blocks.note: first meaning: sturdy, heavily built

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a solidly built person and also names a dark beer brewed with roasted malt.

indicators.note: a tray carrying something holds it on top, so one word sits inside the other

explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat as in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, which is a form of ridicule or farce.

clue.text: Served up in decanter, alcoholic drink

in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of decanter and the start of alcoholic run together

explanation.surface: A drink poured out from a decanter at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The hiding place runs into the word alcoholic, which also colours the surface; the definition itself is simply drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux, a drink often poured from a decanter.

clue.text: Data held by former political office

blocks.note: a party that holds power is said to be in
the Foreign Office, merged in 2020 into a larger department

explanation.surface: Records kept by a government department that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO was the British Foreign Office until it merged with the aid department, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal shortening of information, which is facts or figures, the same thing as data.

clue.text: Idea: it arising in middle of day

blocks.note: noon is midday
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the short word turns upward before going inside the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief held in the mind, so it is a synonym for an idea.

clue.text: Need month off for getting better

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A patient is told to take a month off work to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the mend is recovering from illness or injury, so is improving in health.

clue.text: Extraordinary bird gathering first of twigs

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the next word
gathering in means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a common speckled songbird
the opening letter of twigs

explanation.surface: A remarkable bird collects twigs to build its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' looks like it describes the bird, but it is the definition, an adjective meaning surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising or astonishing, which fits something unusual and remarkable.

blocks.note: first meaning: hit repeatedly and heavily
second meaning: the British unit of money, which is a coin

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like minting money, as one strikes a coin; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to beat hard and also names the British currency unit, minted as a one-pound coin.

clue.text: Heavy food dogs eat, not a liquid

taken as written
the letter to be taken away

explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is British slang for filling, starchy food such as heavy puddings that sit in the stomach.

blocks.note: first meaning: a musical note worth half a crotchet
second meaning: a tremble or wavering in the voice

explanation.walkthrough: A quaver is the British name for an eighth note; the question mark flags that a trill would contain many such short notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a short musical note and also a shaky, tremulous sound in singing or speech.

blocks.note: a book is out once it has been published
a right is something one is entitled to by law

explanation.definitionFit: Outright means complete and unqualified, as in an outright winner, so it describes a clear result.

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to flop down is to sit heavily
an ISA is a British tax-free savings account

explanation.walkthrough: An Individual Savings Account shelters savings from UK tax; both pieces are reversed together, not one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: As it is can mean already, as in 'we have too much to do as it is', referring to the present state.

clue.text: Playwright left piece of material for wrapping up

definitions.text: piece of material for wrapping up

blocks.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dramatist abandons a draft of a script he was finishing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of material' suggests a scrap of writing for the playwright; it is cloth, and 'wrapping up' means keeping warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a large square of fabric worn over the shoulders, used to wrap oneself against the cold.

indicators.note: off implies something out of its normal state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the weekday

explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine generating electricity, used figuratively for a forceful, tireless person.

blocks.note: to do a job with a tool is to do it using that tool
a stand is a posture or position taken up

explanation.surface: Someone poses with a bear, or an animal strikes a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand something is to endure or resist it, the same as to bear pressure or hardship.

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
the closing letter of many

explanation.surface: A small box holding the very last of a large number of items.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means very small in size, a direct synonym of little used as an adjective.

blocks.note: first meaning: a pair, especially of game birds
second meaning: steady oneself before a blow

clue.text: Cup of tea inspiring family activity in kitchen

kin are relatives

explanation.walkthrough: BA(KIN)G. 'Cup of tea' looks like a drink, but it is the idiom for what someone likes, which is also their bag; a teabag is a tempting red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking is cooking food such as bread and cakes in an oven, a typical pastime carried out at home.

clue.text: Some yellow in effect for red or white?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the two common colours of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine comes as red or white (yellow-tinged white included), so the pair of colours stands for the drink by example.

clue.text: Drained wetlands in which frog, say, lies

blocks.note: the first and last letters of wetlands

explanation.walkthrough: W(HOPPER)S. 'Lies' looks like the frog's posture; it is the definition, meaning untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoppers is informal for big, blatant untruths, so the plural noun matches lies.

blocks.note: the sound used to ask for silence

blocks.note: first meaning: a stock of goods made available

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female

blocks.note: a rep, a representative, acts as an agent
taken as written
